descripcion_geo: Nomadic desert people of Negev and Sinai, descendants of Esau. Perennial enemy of Israel in the period of the exodus and the judges.
importancia_estrategica: Israel's first enemy in the desert; control of the steps of the Negev and the Sinai.

historias.descripcion: Amalek attacks Israel fresh from Egypt in Rephidim; Joshua fights while Moses keeps his arms raised.
Saul defeats Amalek but spares King Agag and the best of the cattle; Samuel disapproves and breaks up with him.
While David is at war, Amalekites sack Ziklag; David chases after them and recovers everything they had taken.

personajes.descripcion: He commanded Israel's first battle in the wilderness against Amalek at Rephidim.
His mercy to Agag king of Amalek cost him the kingdom; sign of his disobedience to God.
Forgiven by Saul but executed by Samuel: 'As your sword left women childless, so will your mother be childless.'

contexto_religioso.contexto_lugar: Israel's first adversary in history; symbol of the evil that stalks God's people in the desert. 'War with Amalek from generation to generation' (Ex 17:16).

judaismo.descripcion: The war with Amalek is declared eternal (Ex 17:16); The rabbis identify it as a symbol of radical evil.
judaismo.significado_teologico: The war with Amalek is declared eternal (Ex 17:16); The rabbis identify it as a symbol of radical evil.
